text:
After a routine morning, a missed handover followed pet arrivals at the Companion Animal Travel Desk of Aurelia Skyways. Incident report: delayed transfer of animal service notes during inbound processing. The shift began with standard reception work and the first pet checks ran normally. The issue arose when the outgoing coordinator left before briefing the incoming desk lead on several active bookings and comfort notes. As a result, the initial review of incoming crates and traveler requests was incomplete, and one carrier was directed to the secondary staging area before the full welfare file was opened.

The delay was noticed when the senior coordinator compared the arrival list with the desk log and saw a gap in the handover entries. The welfare coordinator was brought in at once to confirm feed, water, and rest needs for each animal on the desk. A passenger expressed concern about a pet's settling behavior, and the supervisor listened carefully before confirming that the animal was stable and would remain under close observation. No animal was harmed, and no flight was affected, but the missing handover created avoidable confusion for staff and travelers.

I took control of the desk flow, separated the active cases, and restored the notes to the correct order. The team verified the welfare details against the shipping records, checked crate labels, and updated the cabin team so the in-flight monitoring plan matched the revised desk instructions. One pet was kept in a quieter holding space, and water and comfort bedding were confirmed before transfer. The traveler was informed in plain terms that the matter was administrative and that the animal's care remained secure.

Follow-up actions were completed before the shift ended. I instructed the outgoing and incoming coordinators to use a direct face-to-face handover for all live pet movements, and the senior coordinator agreed to reinforce that practice on the next roster. The welfare coordinator will review any animal notes flagged at receipt, and the cabin team will continue to report comfort concerns without delay. The desk log now reflects the full sequence of events, and service has returned to normal. This report is filed for internal review and for improvement of handover discipline.
